title: 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive
summary: The 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive was a significant military operation conducted by the Armed Forces of Ukraine against Russian forces during the [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian war]], commencing on 6 September 2022. This counteroffensive led to the rapid recapture of key territories in Kharkiv Oblast, demonstrating Ukraine's military capabilities and impacting the overall dynamics of the conflict.

title: 2022 Kherson counteroffensive
summary: The 2022 Kherson counteroffensive was a significant military operation launched by Ukraine on 29 August 2022, aimed at reclaiming territories occupied by Russian forces in the southern regions of Kherson and Mykolaiv oblasts. This counteroffensive marked a pivotal phase in the ongoing conflict, leading to the liberation of Kherson, the only regional capital captured by Russia since the invasion began.

title: administrative territorial entity of Ukraine
summary: The administrative territorial entities of Ukraine are defined by the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] Constitution and consist of a unitary state structure with three levels of divisions: regions, raions, and hromadas. This framework is crucial for the governance and administrative organization of Ukraine.
aliases: Administrative and territorial system of Ukraine

title: agriculture in Ukraine
summary: Agriculture in Ukraine is a critical component of the national economy, recognized as one of the largest agricultural producers and exporters globally, often referred to as the 'breadbasket of Europe'. The sector encompasses vast agricultural land and significantly contributes to both domestic food supply and international food security.

title: Anatoliy Solovyanenko
summary: Anatoliy Borysovych Solovianenko was a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] operatic tenor, recognized as a People's Artist of the USSR and Ukraine, and a recipient of the Shevchenko National Prize. His contributions to Ukrainian opera and culture have left a lasting legacy.

title: Andriy Shevchenko
summary: Andriy Mykolayovych Shevchenko is a prominent Ukrainian former football manager and player, widely regarded as one of the greatest strikers in football history and the top scorer for the Ukraine national team. His illustrious career includes significant achievements with clubs like Dynamo Kyiv, AC Milan, and Chelsea, as well as leading Ukraine in international competitions.

title: Antonov
summary: Antonov is a Ukrainian aerospace manufacturer known for its expertise in large aircraft and operations on unprepared runways. Established in 1946 and relocated to Kyiv in 1952, Antonov has produced approximately 22,000 aircraft, significantly impacting both military and civilian aviation.
aliases: Aeronautical Scientific-Technical Complex named after Antonov
Aviatsionny Nauchno-Tekhnichesky Kompleks Imeni O K Antonova
Research and Design Bureau named after O. K. Antonov

title: ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih
summary: ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, formerly known as Kryvorizhstal, is the largest integrated steel company in Ukraine, established in 1934 in Kryvyi Rih. The company plays a significant role in the [[economy-of-ukraine|Ukrainian economy]] as a major producer of steel, particularly rebar and wire rod.

title: Armed Forces of Ukraine
summary: The Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) serve as the military forces of Ukraine, comprising various branches including the Ground Forces, Air Force, Navy, and Special Operations Forces. With a total strength of 4.9 million, the AFU is recognized as one of the largest armed forces globally and plays a critical role in Ukraine's defense, particularly amid ongoing conflicts.

title: bandura
summary: The bandura is a traditional Ukrainian plucked-string folk instrument that merges characteristics of the zither and lute. It has evolved significantly over the centuries, becoming a symbol of Ukrainian cultural heritage and identity.

title: Battle of Bakhmut
summary: The Battle of Bakhmut was a significant confrontation between the Russian Armed Forces and the [[armed-forces-of-ukraine|Ukrainian Armed Forces]] for control of the city of Bakhmut during the Russo-Ukrainian War. It is noted for being one of the bloodiest battles since World War II, with high casualties and intense urban warfare.

title: Battle of Debaltseve
summary: The Battle of Debaltseve was a significant military engagement in January and February 2015, occurring in the city of Debaltseve, Donetsk Oblast, between [[armed-forces-of-ukraine|Ukrainian Armed Forces]] and pro-Russian separatists. This battle was pivotal in the context of the ongoing war in the [[donbas|Donbas]] region, marking the last major confrontation before the Minsk II ceasefire took effect.

title: Battle of Ilovaisk
summary: The Battle of Ilovaisk, which commenced on 7 August 2014, was a significant confrontation between the [[armed-forces-of-ukraine|Armed Forces of Ukraine]] and pro-Russian insurgents, culminating in a tragic encirclement and heavy losses for Ukrainian forces. This battle is a critical event in the context of the ongoing conflict in Eastern Ukraine, highlighting the involvement of Russian military forces and the challenges faced by Ukraine in its defense efforts.

title: Battle of Kyiv
summary: The Battle of Kyiv was a significant military operation during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, aimed at capturing Kyiv, the capital of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. It occurred from 24 February 2022 to 2 April 2022 and concluded with the withdrawal of Russian forces following sustained Ukrainian resistance.

title: Battle of Sievierodonetsk
summary: The Battle of Sievierodonetsk was a significant military engagement during the [[donbas|Donbas]] conflict in eastern Ukraine, part of the broader Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]]. The battle resulted in heavy urban combat, leading to extensive destruction and loss of life, with Sievierodonetsk being a crucial administrative center in Luhansk Oblast.

title: Bohdan Khmelnytsky
summary: Bohdan Khmelnytsky (c. 1595 – 6 August 1657) was a prominent Ruthenian nobleman and military leader of the Zaporozhian [[cossacks|Cossacks]], serving as [[hetman|Hetman]] of the Zaporozhian Host. He is best known for leading a successful uprising against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which resulted in the establishment of an independent Cossack state in [[dnieper|Dnieper]] Ukraine.

title: borscht
summary: Borscht is a sour soup that is particularly associated with [[ukrainian-cuisine|Ukrainian cuisine]], characterized by its use of red beetroots, which impart a distinctive red color. This dish has deep cultural significance in Ukraine and has evolved into various regional interpretations across Eastern Europe.

title: Bucha massacre
summary: The Bucha massacre refers to the mass killing of Ukrainian civilians and prisoners of war by the Russian Armed Forces during the occupation of Bucha, a city near Kyiv, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Documented evidence of the atrocities surfaced on April 1, 2022, following the withdrawal of Russian forces.

title: cabbage roll
summary: Cabbage rolls, known as holubtsi in Ukraine, are a traditional dish that consists of cooked cabbage leaves filled with various ingredients, reflecting the culinary heritage of Central and Eastern Europe, including Ukraine.

title: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine
summary: The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine is the highest executive authority in the country, responsible for implementing state policies and governing various ministries. Established on April 18, 1991, it has undergone several structural changes and is currently led by Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi since July 16, 2026.

title: Carpathians
summary: The Carpathian Mountains, known as Карпати in Ukrainian, are a significant mountain range in Central and Southeast Europe, extending approximately 1,500 km (930 mi) and featuring diverse ecosystems and geological formations. The range plays a crucial role in Ukraine's natural landscape and biodiversity.

title: Chernihiv
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Chernihiv is a city and municipality located in northern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Chernihiv Oblast and Chernihiv Raion. With a population of 282,747 as of 2022, Chernihiv has a rich historical significance, having been an important cultural and political center since the 9th century.

title: Chernivtsi
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Chernivtsi is a city of regional significance in southwestern Ukraine, located on the upper course of the Prut River. Historically the capital of Bukovina, the city has played a vital role in the cultural and administrative landscape of Ukraine.

title: Chernobyl disaster
summary: The Chernobyl disaster, which occurred on April 26, 1986, at reactor 4 of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant near Pripyat, Ukraine, is one of the most catastrophic nuclear accidents in history. It resulted in immediate fatalities and long-term health issues, marking a significant event in Ukraine's history and impacting nuclear safety worldwide.

title: Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant
summary: The Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant (ChNPP) is a decommissioning nuclear power facility located in northern Ukraine, near the city of Pripyat. It is historically significant due to the catastrophic disaster that occurred in 1986, which has had lasting impacts on nuclear safety and environmental policy in Ukraine and beyond.
aliases: Vladimir Ilyich Lenin Nuclear Power Plant

title: Constitution of Ukraine
summary: The Constitution of Ukraine, adopted on 28 June 1996, serves as the fundamental law of Ukraine, establishing the framework for the country's governance and legal system. It is significant for its role in defining the rights of citizens and the structure of the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]].

title: Constitutional Court of Ukraine
summary: The Constitutional Court of Ukraine is the highest judicial authority responsible for interpreting the [[constitution-of-ukraine|Constitution of Ukraine]] and ensuring the constitutionality of laws and legal acts. Established on 18 October 1996, the Court plays a crucial role in the Ukrainian legal system, with its decisions being binding and final.

title: Cossack Hetmanate
type: vassal and tributary state of the Ottoman Empire
summary: The Cossack Hetmanate, officially known as the Zaporozhian Host, was a stratocratic state established by Registered [[cossacks|Cossacks]] in Dnieper Ukraine, existing from 1648 to 1764. It played a significant role in Ukrainian history, particularly through its interactions with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Tsardom of Moscow.

title: Cossacks
summary: The Cossacks are a significant social class in [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] history, primarily composed of East Slavic, Eastern Orthodox Christian individuals who originated from the Pontic–Caspian steppe. They played a crucial role in military defense and the development of the southern [[administrative-territorial-entity-of-ukraine|regions of Ukraine]] and surrounding areas.

title: Crimea
summary: Crimea is a peninsula located in Eastern Europe, bordered by the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, and is internationally recognized as part of Ukraine. The region has a complex history marked by various cultures and powers, and has been under Russian occupation since 2014.

title: Crimean Tatars
summary: Crimean Tatars are an Eastern European Turkic ethnic group indigenous to Crimea, with a rich history shaped by various migrations and cultural influences. Their population and cultural identity have faced significant challenges, particularly during the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union, yet they remain a vital part of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s demographic and cultural landscape.

title: Crimean War
summary: The Crimean War was a significant conflict fought from October 1853 to February 1856 between Russia and an alliance of the Ottoman Empire, France, the United Kingdom, and Sardinia. Its implications extended to Ukraine, particularly through the involvement of the Black Sea region and the geopolitical dynamics that shaped the area during this period.

title: Cucuteni–Trypillia culture
summary: The Cucuteni–Trypillia culture is a Neolithic–Chalcolithic archaeological culture that thrived from approximately 5050 to 2950 BC in Southeast Europe, particularly in regions of modern-day Ukraine. It is notable for its large settlements, advanced agricultural practices, and significant contributions to early urban development.

title: culture of Ukraine
summary: The culture of Ukraine encompasses the material and spiritual values of its people, shaped by a rich history that includes strong family ties, religious influences, and traditional arts. This culture has persisted through various historical challenges and has seen a revival since Ukraine's independence in 1991.

title: Denys Shmyhal
summary: Denys Anatoliiovych Shmyhal, born on 15 October 1975, is a prominent Ukrainian politician and entrepreneur who served as the 18th Prime Minister of Ukraine from 2020 to 2025. His political career includes significant roles in managing Ukraine's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the defense during the 2022 Russian invasion.

title: Dnieper
summary: The Dnieper, also known as the Dnipro, is a significant transboundary river in Europe, originating in Russia and flowing through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea. It is the longest river in Ukraine and plays a crucial role in the country's economy and cultural identity.

title: Dniester
summary: The Dniester is a transboundary river in Eastern Europe, primarily flowing through Ukraine before continuing into Moldova and discharging into the Black Sea on Ukrainian territory. It serves as a significant geographical and historical landmark in the region.

title: Dnipro
summary: Dnipro is the fourth-largest city in Ukraine, located in the eastern part of the country along the Dnipro River. With a population of approximately one million, it serves as the administrative center of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and has a rich historical and industrial significance.

title: Donbas
summary: The Donbas is a historically significant industrial region located on the border between Russia and Ukraine, primarily within Ukraine itself. It has been a crucial coal mining area since the late 19th century and has been impacted by ongoing geopolitical conflicts, particularly the Russo-Ukrainian war.

title: Donetsk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Donetsk is an industrial city in eastern Ukraine, situated on the Kalmius River within Donetsk Oblast. Historically significant as the unofficial capital of the [[donbas|Donets Basin]], it has been a focal point of conflict during the Russo-Ukrainian War since 2014.

title: DTEK
summary: DTEK is the largest private investor in Ukraine's energy sector, involved in electricity generation, coal and gas extraction, and energy trading. The company plays a crucial role in the development of renewable energy and supports Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

title: economy of Ukraine
summary: The economy of Ukraine is characterized as a developing social market economy, featuring rich agricultural land, a diverse industrial base, and significant mineral resources. Despite these advantages, Ukraine faces challenges such as high corruption levels and slow economic reforms, contributing to its status as one of the poorest countries in Europe.

title: Energoatom
summary: Energoatom is the state-owned enterprise responsible for operating all nuclear power plants in Ukraine, making it the largest electricity producer in the country. Founded in October 1996, it plays a crucial role in meeting Ukraine's energy needs and ensuring nuclear safety.

title: Euromaidan
summary: Euromaidan, also known as the Maidan Uprising, was a significant wave of protests and civil unrest in Ukraine that began on 21 November 2013. Triggered by President [[viktor-yanukovych|Viktor Yanukovych]]'s decision to reject the European Union–Ukraine Association Agreement in favor of closer ties with Russia, the movement highlighted widespread discontent with government corruption and human rights violations, ultimately leading to the 2014 Revolution of Dignity.

title: Executed Renaissance
summary: The Executed Renaissance refers to a generation of Ukrainian artists and intellectuals active during the 1920s and early 1930s in the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, whose cultural contributions were largely suppressed during [[donetsk|Stalin]]'s Great Terror. This period was marked by significant advancements in various artistic fields, ultimately leading to the tragic loss of many of its key figures.

title: foreign relations of Ukraine
summary: The foreign relations of Ukraine encompass its diplomatic engagements with various nations, emphasizing Euro-Atlantic integration and security partnerships, particularly in response to regional threats. Ukraine's foreign policy has evolved significantly, especially following the annexation of Crimea and the ongoing conflict with Russia.

title: full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war
summary: The full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war began on 24 February 2022 with Russia's invasion of Ukraine, marking the most significant military conflict in Europe since World War II. This war escalated from earlier hostilities that started in 2014 when Russia annexed Crimea and supported separatist movements in eastern Ukraine.

title: hetman
summary: Hetman is a historical political and military title from Central and Eastern Europe, particularly significant in Ukraine as the title of the head of the Cossack state following the [[khmelnytsky-uprising|Khmelnytsky Uprising]] of 1648. The title has roots in various cultures and has evolved over time, reflecting the military and political landscape of the region.

title: Holodomor
summary: The Holodomor, or Ukrainian famine, was a catastrophic man-made famine that occurred in Soviet Ukraine from 1932 to 1933, resulting in the deaths of millions of Ukrainians. This event is a significant part of Ukraine's history and has been recognized by various nations as a genocide against the Ukrainian people.

title: hopak
summary: Hopak is a traditional Ukrainian folk dance that originated as a male dance among the Zaporozhian Cossacks and has evolved to include couples and mixed groups. It is often celebrated as the 'National Dance of Ukraine' and is performed by various dance ensembles both in Ukraine and internationally.

title: hryvnia
summary: The hryvnia is the official currency of Ukraine, introduced on 2 September 1996. It is subdivided into 100 kopiyka and is named after a historical measure of weight from Kievan Rus'.

title: Interpipe Group
summary: Interpipe Group is a Ukrainian industrial company recognized as a global manufacturer of steel pipes and railway wheels, with its headquarters and production facilities situated in Nikopol, Ukraine. The company plays a significant role in the carbon steel pipes and railway products markets, employing approximately 11,000 individuals.

title: Ivan Franko
summary: Ivan Yakovych Franko was a prominent Ukrainian poet, writer, and political activist, recognized as a key figure in the development of modern Ukrainian literature and socialist thought. His contributions include pioneering detective novels and modern poetry, as well as translating significant works into Ukrainian.

title: Ivano-Frankivsk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Ivano-Frankivsk is a city of regional significance in [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]], serving as the administrative center of Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast and Ivano-Frankivsk Raion. With a population of approximately 238,196 in 2022, it has a rich historical background and diverse cultural influences.

title: Jamala
summary: Susana Alimivna Jamaladinova, known as Jamala, is a prominent Ukrainian singer who gained international recognition by winning the Eurovision Song Contest in 2016 with her song '1944'. Her work is deeply connected to her Crimean Tatar heritage and the historical context of Crimea, particularly the deportation of the Crimean Tatars.

title: Kerch Strait incident
summary: The Kerch Strait incident, occurring on 25 November 2018, involved the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) coast guard firing upon and capturing three Ukrainian Navy vessels as they attempted to transit from the Black Sea to the Sea of Azov. This event marked the first direct engagement between Russian and Ukrainian forces during the ongoing [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian War]] and highlighted the tensions surrounding maritime access to Ukrainian ports.

title: Kharkiv
summary: Kharkiv, the second-largest city in Ukraine, serves as the administrative center of Kharkiv Oblast and Kharkiv Raion. It has a rich history as a cultural, industrial, and educational hub, significantly influencing the development of Ukrainian identity and politics.

title: Kherson
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Kherson is a significant port city in southern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Kherson Oblast. Established in the late 18th century, it has been an important hub for shipbuilding and trade, with a population of approximately 279,131 as of early 2022.

title: Khmelnytsky Uprising
summary: The Khmelnytsky Uprising was a significant Cossack rebellion that occurred between 1648 and 1657 in the eastern territories of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, primarily in [[dnieper|Dnieper]] Ukraine. Led by Cossack Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky, the uprising resulted in a Cossack victory and the establishment of the Cossack Hetmanate, marking a pivotal moment in Ukraine's history and its relations with Poland and Russia.

title: Kievan Rus'
summary: Kievan Rus', also referred to as Kyivan Rus', was the inaugural East Slavic state and a collective of principalities in Eastern Europe from the late 9th to the mid-13th century. It played a crucial role in shaping the cultural and political landscape of Ukraine and the surrounding region.

title: Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia
summary: The Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia, also referred to as the Kingdom of Ruthenia or Kingdom of Rus', was a significant medieval state in Eastern Europe that existed from 1199 to 1349, primarily within the territory of modern-day [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. It emerged from the fragmentation of [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]' and played a crucial role in the region's political landscape during its existence.

title: Kolomyjka
summary: Kolomyika is a [[music-of-ukraine|Ukrainian music]] genre characterized by a lively folk dance and humorous rhymed verses. Originating from the town of Kolomyia in western Ukraine, it has historical significance among Ukrainians and Poles and continues to be a vibrant part of cultural festivities in Ukraine.

title: Kramatorsk railway station attack
summary: The Kramatorsk railway station attack occurred on 8 April 2022, when a Russian missile strike targeted civilians in Kramatorsk, Ukraine, resulting in 63 fatalities, including 9 children, and 150 injuries. This incident highlights the ongoing violence during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which began on 24 February 2022.

title: Kryvyi Rih
summary: Kryvyi Rih is a significant city located in central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Kryvyi Rih Raion in [[dnipro|Dnipropetrovsk]] Oblast. With a population of approximately 603,904 as of 2022, it ranks as the seventh-most populous city in Ukraine and is notable for its extensive industrial history and geographical features.

title: Kutia
summary: Kutia, also known as kutya, is a ceremonial grain dish in syrup that holds significant cultural importance in [[ukrainian-cuisine|Ukrainian cuisine]], particularly during the Christmas season. It is traditionally made with wheatberries, poppy seeds, and honey, reflecting ancient rituals and customs.

title: Kyiv
summary: Kyiv, the capital and largest city of Ukraine, is situated in the north-central region of the country along both banks of the Dnieper River. With a population of 2,952,301 as of January 2022, it serves as a significant industrial, scientific, educational, and cultural hub in Ukraine and Eastern Europe.

title: Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
summary: The Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, also known as the Kyiv Monastery of the Caves, is a significant Eastern Orthodox monastery located in Kyiv, Ukraine. Founded in 1051, it has played a crucial role in the history of Eastern Christianity in Eastern Europe.

title: Kyiv Zhuliany International Airport
summary: Kyiv Zhuliany International Airport, officially known as Igor Sikorsky Kyiv International Airport, is one of the two main passenger airports serving the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv. Located approximately seven kilometers southwest of the city center, it plays a significant role in both passenger and business aviation in Ukraine.

title: Kyivstar
summary: Kyivstar is a prominent Ukrainian telecommunications operator providing a range of voice and data services, including 4G LTE, across Ukraine. As of 2024, it serves approximately 24 million mobile subscribers and has expanded its services to include partnerships with international entities such as Starlink.

title: Leonid Kravchuk
summary: Leonid Makarovych Kravchuk was a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the first [[president-of-ukraine|president of Ukraine]] from December 5, 1991, to July 19, 1994, playing a crucial role in the country's independence from the Soviet Union. His presidency was marked by significant political and economic challenges, including the management of Ukraine's nuclear arsenal and a severe economic crisis.

title: Leonid Kuchma
summary: Leonid Danylovych Kuchma is a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the second president of Ukraine from 19 July 1994 to 23 January 2005. His presidency is noted for economic stabilization and improved relations with Russia, but also for democratic backsliding and increased oligarchic influence.

title: Lesya Ukrainka
summary: Lesya Ukrainka, born Larysa Petrivna Kosach on 25 February 1871, was a prominent Ukrainian writer known for her poetry and plays, as well as her activism for political, civil, and women's rights. Her works and life are deeply intertwined with the cultural and historical context of Ukraine.

title: Luhansk
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Luhansk is a city of regional significance located in eastern [[ukraine|Ukraine]], specifically within the Donbas region. As of 2022, it is the 12th-largest city in Ukraine, with a population of approximately 397,677.

title: Lviv
summary: Lviv is the fifth-largest city in Ukraine and the largest in the western region, with an estimated population of 723,403 in 2025. It serves as the administrative center of Lviv Oblast and is recognized as a key cultural hub in Ukraine.

title: Maidan Nezalezhnosti
summary: Maidan Nezalezhnosti, or Independence Square, is the central square of Kyiv, Ukraine, significant for its role in political movements and as a symbol of [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] independence. It features the Independence Monument and has been the site of numerous historic protests and events since the 1990s.

title: Mariupol
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Mariupol is a city of regional significance located in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine, on the northern coast of the Sea of Azov. Historically an industrial and trade center, it has faced significant challenges, particularly during the [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian War]].

title: Mariupol theatre airstrike
summary: The Mariupol theatre airstrike occurred on 16 March 2022 during the Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]], targeting a building used as an air raid shelter for civilians. This attack has been classified as a war crime by various organizations due to the high number of civilian casualties and the deliberate nature of the bombing.

title: Metinvest
summary: Metinvest is a prominent group of steel and mining companies with significant operations in Ukraine and other countries. It is recognized as Ukraine's largest producer of iron ore and steel, playing a vital role in the nation's economy.

title: Minsk agreements
summary: The Minsk agreements were a series of international accords aimed at resolving the conflict in Eastern Ukraine, specifically the Donbas War, which involved armed Russian separatists and the [[armed-forces-of-ukraine|Armed Forces of Ukraine]]. The agreements, known as Minsk I and Minsk II, sought to establish ceasefires and outline steps for peace, but faced numerous violations and challenges, significantly impacting Ukraine's territorial integrity and security.

title: modern history of Ukraine
summary: The modern history of Ukraine is marked by its evolution from a region under imperial control to an independent nation-state, characterized by significant events such as the Ukrainian National Revival, the struggle for independence, Soviet rule, and ongoing conflicts in the post-Soviet era.

title: Moskva
summary: Moskva, previously known as Slava, was a guided missile cruiser of the Russian Navy, commissioned in 1983 and serving as the flagship of the Black Sea Fleet. Its involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian War, particularly during the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, marked a significant chapter in its operational history.

title: Motor Sich
summary: Motor Sich, Joint Stock Company, is a prominent Ukrainian aircraft engine manufacturer located in Zaporizhzhia, specializing in engines for airplanes, helicopters, and industrial marine gas turbines.

title: music of Ukraine
summary: The music of Ukraine encompasses a rich tapestry of influences from both Western and Eastern European traditions, deeply rooted in indigenous Slavic and Christian elements. It reflects the country's historical significance as a cultural hub within the former Russian Empire and showcases a diverse array of folk and classical music forms.

title: Mykhailo Hrushevskyi
summary: Mykhailo Hrushevskyi was a prominent Ukrainian historian, politician, and statesman, recognized as a key figure in the Ukrainian national revival of the early 20th century. His contributions to Ukrainian history and culture, particularly through his extensive writings and political activism, have left a lasting impact on Ukraine's national identity.

title: Mykolaiv
summary: Mykolaiv is a significant port city and administrative center in southern Ukraine, known for its strategic location at the confluence of the Inhul and Southern Bug rivers. It is recognized as a key shipbuilding hub and has been impacted by historical events, including the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

title: Naftogaz of Ukraine
summary: Naftogaz of Ukraine is the largest state-owned oil and gas company in Ukraine, responsible for the complete cycle of natural gas and crude oil operations. The company plays a crucial role in Ukraine's energy sector and has significant influence in regional politics due to its infrastructure connecting Russia and the European Union.

title: National Bank of Ukraine
summary: The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) serves as the central bank of Ukraine, established in 1991 from the Soviet Gosbank's Ukrainian operations. It plays a crucial role in regulating the country's financial system and ensuring the stability of the national currency, the Hryvnia.

title: Nova Post
summary: Nova Poshta, known as Nova Post outside Ukraine, is a private postal and courier service based in Ukraine, providing logistics solutions for both individuals and businesses. Established in 2001, it has grown to become a significant player in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] market, competing primarily with Ukrposhta.

title: Odesa
summary: Odesa, a significant port city in Ukraine, is the third-most populous municipality in the country and serves as a vital transport hub on the Black Sea. Its rich history, multicultural heritage, and recent recognition as a World Heritage Site underscore its importance in the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] context.

title: Oleh Blokhin
summary: Oleh Blokhin is a prominent Ukrainian former football player and manager, celebrated as one of the greatest footballers of his generation. He holds numerous records in Ukrainian and Soviet football, including being the all-time top goalscorer for both Dynamo Kyiv and the Soviet Union national team.

title: Oleksandr Turchynov
summary: Oleksandr Turchynov is a prominent Ukrainian politician, economist, and Baptist minister, known for his roles in the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]], including serving as acting President and Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council. His political career has been significantly intertwined with key events in Ukraine's recent history, particularly during the 2014 political crisis and the ongoing conflict with Russia.

title: Olga Kurylenko
summary: Olga Kostyantynivna Kurylenko is a Ukrainian-French actress and former model, known for her role as Camille Montes in the James Bond film Quantum of Solace (2008). Born in Berdyansk, Ukraine, she has gained international recognition through her diverse filmography and significant contributions to cinema.

title: Orange Revolution
summary: The Orange Revolution was a series of protests in Ukraine from late November 2004 to January 2005, initiated by widespread public discontent over perceived electoral fraud in the presidential election. The movement ultimately led to the annulment of the election results and a re-vote, resulting in Viktor Yushchenko's presidency.

title: Oschadbank
summary: Oschadbank, officially known as Public JSC 'State Savings Bank of Ukraine', is a significant public bank in Ukraine recognized as one of the country's systemically important banks. Established after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Oschadbank plays a crucial role in the Ukrainian banking sector, providing various financial services across its extensive branch and ATM network.

title: paska
summary: Paska is a traditional Ukrainian Easter bread that holds cultural significance in Ukraine and other Central and Eastern European countries with ties to the Byzantine Empire and Eastern Christianity. It is an essential part of Easter celebrations, symbolizing the resurrection of Christ and featuring prominently in various festive customs.

title: Petro Poroshenko
summary: Petro Oleksiiovych Poroshenko is a prominent Ukrainian politician and businessman who served as the fifth president of Ukraine from 2014 to 2019. His leadership was marked by significant military and economic reforms, as well as a strong push for Ukraine's integration with the European Union.

title: Petrykivka painting
summary: Petrykivka painting is a traditional Ukrainian decorative art form that originated in the village of Petrykivka, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. Recognized for its vibrant floral patterns and unique brush techniques, this style has been an integral part of Ukrainian culture since the 18th century and continues to evolve as a modern art form.

title: Poltava
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Poltava is a city located on the Vorskla River in Central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Poltava Oblast and Poltava Raion. With an estimated population of 279,593 in 2022, it holds significant historical and cultural relevance in Ukraine.

title: potato pancake
summary: Potato pancakes, known in Ukraine as деруни (deruny), are shallow-fried pancakes made primarily from grated potatoes, often combined with ingredients like flour and eggs. This dish is a staple in [[ukrainian-cuisine|Ukrainian cuisine]] and is celebrated for its simplicity and flavor.

title: President of Ukraine
summary: The President of Ukraine serves as the head of state, representing the nation in international affairs and overseeing the executive branch of government. Elected by the citizens for a five-year term, the office has been pivotal in shaping Ukraine's political landscape since its establishment in 1991.

title: Prime Minister of Ukraine
summary: The Prime Minister of Ukraine serves as the head of government, overseeing the Cabinet of Ministers, the highest executive body in the country. This position has evolved since Ukraine's independence in 1991, with various notable individuals holding the office, including the first female prime minister, Yulia Tymoshenko.

title: PrivatBank
summary: PrivatBank is the largest bank in Ukraine by assets, established on 19 March 1992. It has been state-owned since its nationalization in 2016 and is recognized as one of the country's systemically important banks.

title: pysanka
summary: Pysanka is a traditional Ukrainian practice of egg decoration, particularly associated with Easter, that has roots in both pagan and Christian customs. This art form, characterized by intricate designs created using a wax-resist technique, is recognized as a national symbol of Ukraine and has influenced various cultural practices both domestically and internationally.

title: rag doll
summary: A rag doll is a type of doll crafted from fabric scraps, historically serving as both a toy and a tool for teaching sewing skills. In Ukraine, the motanka doll represents a traditional variant of the rag doll, deeply rooted in folk culture and magical beliefs.

title: Revolution of Dignity
summary: The Revolution of Dignity, also known as the Maidan Revolution, occurred in Ukraine in February 2014 as a culmination of the Euromaidan protests. This civil disorder led to the ousting of President Viktor Yanukovych and significant political changes in Ukraine, ultimately contributing to the Russo-Ukrainian war.

title: Roshen
summary: Roshen Confectionery Corporation is a prominent Ukrainian confectionery manufacturing group, known for its extensive production and export of various confectionery products. Founded in 1993, the company has become a significant player in the global candy industry, with its operations deeply rooted in Ukraine.

title: Rushnyk
summary: A rushnyk is a decorative and ritual cloth significant in Ukrainian culture, often made of linen or cotton and featuring intricate woven or embroidered designs. It plays a vital role in various East Slavic rituals, including weddings and funerals, and serves as a symbol of cultural heritage.

title: Ruslana Lyzhychko
summary: Ruslana Stepanivna Lyzhychko, born on 24 May 1973 in Lviv, Ukraine, is a prominent Ukrainian singer, songwriter, producer, activist, and former politician. She gained international fame after winning the Eurovision Song Contest in 2004 and is recognized as one of the most successful Ukrainian female artists globally.

title: Russian annexation of Crimea
summary: The Russian annexation of Crimea occurred in 2014, following an invasion of the peninsula, which is part of Ukraine. This event marked a significant escalation in the ongoing [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|Russo-Ukrainian war]] and has been widely condemned by Ukraine and the international community as a violation of international law.

title: Russo-Ukrainian war
summary: The Russo-Ukrainian war, which commenced in February 2014, has significantly impacted Ukraine following the occupation and [[russian-annexation-of-crimea|annexation of Crimea by Russia]]. The conflict has evolved through various phases, including support for separatist movements in eastern Ukraine and a full-scale invasion by Russia in February 2022, marking the largest military conflict in Europe since World War II.
aliases: Special operation on the territory of Ukraine

title: salo
summary: Salo, also known as slanina, is a traditional European food made from salt-cured pork fat, particularly significant in [[ukrainian-cuisine|Ukrainian cuisine]]. It is characterized by its preparation methods and cultural importance across Central, Eastern, and Southeastern Europe.

title: Security Service of Ukraine
summary: The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) is the primary internal security agency of Ukraine, tasked with counter-intelligence, organized crime, and terrorism prevention. Established in 1991 following Ukraine's independence, the SBU has undergone significant changes in its structure and operations, particularly after the Revolution of Dignity in 2014.

title: Sergei Bubka
summary: Serhiy Nazarovych Bubka is a distinguished Ukrainian former pole vaulter, recognized as the 1988 Olympic Champion and a record six-time consecutive World Champion. His remarkable achievements in athletics and contributions to sports governance have made him a significant figure in Ukraine's sporting history.

title: Servant of the People
summary: Servant of the People is a liberal, centrist political party in [[ukraine|Ukraine]], known for its association with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Since the 2019 elections, it has held a ruling position in the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]].

title: Sevastopol
summary: Sevastopol is the largest city in [[crimea|Crimea]] and a significant port on the Black Sea, founded in 1783 by Catherine the Great. The city has a complex history marked by its strategic military importance and its contentious status following the annexation of Crimea by Russia in 2014, despite being internationally recognized as part of Ukraine.

title: Sich Riflemen
summary: The Sich Riflemen Halych-Bukovyna Kurin was a significant military unit of the [[ukrainians|Ukrainian People]]'s Army, active from 1917 to 1919. Composed of Ukrainian soldiers from the Austro-Hungarian army and local volunteers, the unit played a crucial role in Ukraine's struggle for independence during the tumultuous period following World War I.

title: Siege of Mariupol
summary: The Siege of Mariupol, which commenced on 24 February 2022 and concluded on 20 May 2022, was a critical military engagement during the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The siege resulted in significant casualties and destruction, marking a pivotal moment in the conflict over control of southeastern Ukraine.

title: Snake Island campaign
summary: The Snake Island campaign refers to the Russian military's attack and subsequent occupation of Snake Island, a strategically significant Ukrainian island in the Black Sea, beginning on 24 February 2022, the first day of the Russian [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]]. The campaign lasted for 126 days and involved notable Ukrainian resistance and counteroffensive actions.

title: Sofia Rotaru
summary: Sofiia Mykhailivna Yevdokymenko-Rotaru, commonly known as Sofia Rotaru, is a prominent [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] singer born on 7 August 1947. She has made significant contributions to the music scene in Ukraine and the former Soviet Union, achieving international recognition through her diverse repertoire and performances.

title: Sumy
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Sumy is a city of regional significance located in northeastern Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Sumy Oblast. Founded in the 1650s by [[cossacks|Cossacks]], Sumy has evolved into a significant industrial and cultural hub in Northern Ukraine, with a population of 256,474 as of 2022.

title: Taras Shevchenko
summary: Taras Hryhorovych Shevchenko (9 March 1814 – 10 March 1861) was a prominent Ukrainian poet, writer, artist, and political figure, whose works are foundational to modern Ukrainian literature and language. His literary and artistic contributions have made him a significant cultural icon in Ukraine and among Slavic nations.

title: Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv
summary: The Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv is a prominent public university located in Kyiv, Ukraine, recognized as the third-oldest university in the country. Established in 1834, it has evolved into a leading center for education and research, named after the influential Ukrainian poet and artist Taras Shevchenko.
aliases: Kyiv National University named after Taras Shevchenko

title: Ternopil
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Ternopil, formerly known as Tarnopol until 1944, is a significant city in western Ukraine, situated along the Seret River. As a key urban center in the historical regions of Galicia and Podolia, Ternopil plays an important role in the cultural and administrative landscape of Ukraine.

title: Treaty of Pereyaslav
summary: The Treaty of Pereyaslav, signed in January 1654 in central Ukraine, marked a significant pledge of allegiance by the Zaporozhian Cossacks to the Russian Tsar Alexis I. This agreement, stemming from the Khmelnytsky Uprising, established a complex relationship between the Cossack Hetmanate and the Tsardom of Russia, influencing Ukraine's political landscape for centuries.

title: trembita
summary: The trembita is a wooden alpine horn traditionally associated with the Hutsul highlanders of [[western-ukraine|western Ukraine]]. It serves both musical and signaling purposes within the cultural practices of the region.

title: Ukraine
summary: Ukraine is a sovereign state located in Eastern Europe, recognized as the second-largest country in Europe. It has a rich historical legacy, marked by early human settlement, the establishment of Kievan Rus', and significant events leading to its independence in 1991.

title: Ukraine-NATO relations
summary: Ukraine-NATO relations have evolved significantly since Ukraine's independence in 1991, marked by a series of cooperative agreements and increasing aspirations for NATO membership, particularly following Russian aggression in 2014 and 2022.

title: Ukraine–European Union relations
summary: Ukraine–European Union relations are defined by the Ukraine–European Union Association Agreement and the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area (DCFTA), highlighting Ukraine's strategic partnership with the EU. The relationship has evolved significantly, culminating in Ukraine being granted candidate status for EU accession in June 2022.

title: Ukrainian
summary: Ukrainian is an East Slavic language predominantly spoken in Ukraine, serving as the native language for a significant majority of its population. The language has evolved through various historical phases, influenced by neighboring languages and cultures, and is characterized by its unique phonetic and grammatical features.

title: Ukrainian Carpathians
summary: The Ukrainian Carpathians are a segment of the Eastern Carpathians located in the southwestern part of Ukraine, spanning four administrative regions. This mountain range is significant for its diverse geological features and cultural relevance within Ukraine.

title: Ukrainian cuisine
summary: Ukrainian cuisine encompasses the diverse culinary traditions of Ukraine, influenced by its fertile soil and historical agricultural practices. It features a range of traditional dishes, with red borscht recognized as the national dish, and reflects the country's cultural heritage and regional similarities within Eastern European cuisine.

title: Ukrainian Defense Industry
summary: The Ukrainian Defense Industry, known as Ukroboronprom, is the largest arms manufacturer in Ukraine and ranks among the top 50 companies in the global arms sector. Established in 2010, it has adapted its operations in response to the ongoing conflict with Russia, including relocating parts of its production abroad since the 2022 invasion.

title: Ukrainian diaspora
summary: The Ukrainian diaspora consists of Ukrainians and their descendants living outside [[ukraine|Ukraine]], who often maintain connections to their ancestral homeland and a sense of Ukrainian national identity. This diaspora is widespread, particularly in post-Soviet states, North America, and parts of Europe and South America.

title: Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church
summary: The Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church (UGCC) is an autonomous Eastern Catholic church based in Ukraine, in full communion with the Holy See. It traces its origins to the Christianization of [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]' in 988 and has played a significant role in the development of Ukrainian identity and culture.
aliases: Ukrainian Catholic Church of the Byzantine Tradition

title: Ukrainian Ground Forces
summary: The Ukrainian Ground Forces, also known as the Ukrainian Army, is the land force component of the [[armed-forces-of-ukraine|Armed Forces of Ukraine]]. Established from Soviet military units following Ukraine's independence, it has undergone significant modernization and expansion, particularly in response to ongoing conflicts in the region.

title: Ukrainian Insurgent Army
summary: The Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) was a nationalist military formation established on 14 October 1942 by the Banderite faction of the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists. It played a significant role in [[ukraine|Ukraine]]'s struggle for independence during World War II, engaging in guerrilla warfare against both Soviet and Nazi forces until the 1950s.

title: Ukrainian literature
summary: Ukrainian literature encompasses literary works written in the Ukrainian language and those created within the territory of Ukraine, reflecting the country's historical and cultural context. Its development has been shaped significantly by foreign dominations and the evolution of the Ukrainian language as a medium for literary expression.

title: Ukrainian Orthodox Church
summary: The Ukrainian Orthodox Church encompasses various Orthodox Christian entities within Ukraine and abroad, reflecting the religious diversity and historical developments of Orthodoxy in the region.

title: Ukrainian People's Republic
summary: The Ukrainian People's Republic (UPR) was a historical state in Eastern Europe that emerged during a period of national awakening in Ukraine following the February Revolution of 1917. It declared independence from Russia on 22 January 1918, amidst a backdrop of conflict involving various factions during the Ukrainian War of Independence.

title: Ukrainian Railways
summary: Ukrainian Railways, officially known as Public JSC Ukrainian Railways or PAT 'Ukrzaliznytsia (UZ)', is a state-owned company responsible for managing railway infrastructure and transportation in Ukraine. It is a significant player in the global rail transport sector, ranking as the sixth largest passenger transporter and seventh largest freight transporter worldwide.

title: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
summary: The Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic (Ukrainian SSR) was a key constituent republic of the Soviet Union from 1922 until 1991, playing a significant role in Ukraine's historical and political landscape. Governed by the Communist Party of the Soviet Union through its Ukrainian branch, the republic underwent numerous territorial and political changes during its existence.

title: Ukrainian War of Independence
summary: The Ukrainian War of Independence, also known as the Ukrainian–Soviet War, occurred from March 1917 to November 1921, forming a significant part of the Russian Civil War and leading to the establishment of an independent Ukrainian republic. This conflict involved various factions vying for control over Ukraine, ultimately resulting in the incorporation of much of the territory into the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic.

title: Ukrainians
summary: Ukrainians are an East Slavic ethnic group primarily associated with Ukraine, where they constitute over three-quarters of the population. With a global population of approximately 46 million, they are the second largest Slavic ethnic group after Russians.

title: Ukrainization
summary: Ukrainization is a policy aimed at promoting the Ukrainian language and culture across various public domains in Ukraine, as well as assimilating non-Ukrainians into Ukrainian cultural practices. This process has historical roots and has evolved through different political contexts in Ukraine.

title: Ukrnafta
summary: Public JSC Ukrnafta is the largest oil and natural gas extraction company in Ukraine, also managing a significant network of gas filling stations. Established in 1994, it plays a crucial role in the country's energy sector and has undergone significant changes in governance and ownership.

title: varenyky
summary: Varenyky are traditional Ukrainian dumplings made from unleavened dough filled with various ingredients, making them a significant part of Ukrainian cuisine and culture.

title: Verkhovna Rada
summary: The Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine serves as the unicameral parliament of the nation, consisting of 450 deputies and located in Kyiv. It has evolved from historical legislative bodies and plays a crucial role in shaping Ukraine's laws and policies.

title: Viktor Yanukovych
summary: Viktor Fedorovych Yanukovych, born on 9 July 1950, is a former Ukrainian politician who served as the fourth [[president-of-ukraine|president of Ukraine]] from 2010 to 2014. His political career was marked by significant events including the 2014 [[revolution-of-dignity|Revolution of Dignity]], which led to his removal from office and subsequent exile in Russia.

title: Viktor Yushchenko
summary: Viktor Andriiovych Yushchenko is a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the third president of Ukraine from 23 January 2005 to 25 February 2010, known for his pro-Western orientation and leadership during pivotal moments in Ukraine's political history.

title: Vinnytsia
summary: Vinnytsia is a city in west-central Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Vinnytsia Oblast and Vinnytsia Raion. With a population of 431,319 as of July 2026, it is the largest city in the historic region of Podillia and has a rich history dating back to the Middle Ages.

title: Vitali Klitschko
summary: Vitali Klitschko is a prominent Ukrainian politician and former professional boxer, serving as the mayor of Kyiv since 2014. He is recognized for his significant contributions to both sports and politics in Ukraine, particularly during the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
summary: Volodymyr Oleksandrovych Zelenskyy is a prominent Ukrainian politician and former entertainer, serving as the sixth [[president-of-ukraine|president of Ukraine]] since 2019. His presidency has been marked by significant challenges, including the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian war and efforts to unify the country's diverse population.

title: vyshyvanka
summary: Vyshyvanka refers to the embroidered shirt integral to Ukrainian and Belarusian national costumes, characterized by unique regional embroidery styles. This garment serves not only as traditional attire but also as a symbol of cultural identity and patriotism in Ukraine.

title: War in Donbas
summary: The war in Donbas, a significant phase of the Russo-Ukrainian war, erupted in April 2014 in the eastern region of Ukraine, marked by a conflict between Russian-backed paramilitaries and the Ukrainian government. This conflict led to the establishment of self-proclaimed republics and continued until it was overshadowed by the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title: West Ukrainian People's Republic
summary: The West Ukrainian People's Republic (ZUNR) was a short-lived state that existed from November 1918 to July 1919, primarily in the region of Galicia. It emerged during the disintegration of Austria-Hungary and sought to establish Ukrainian autonomy amid competing claims from Poland.

title: Western Ukraine
summary: Western Ukraine, known as Zakhidna Ukrayina in Ukrainian, encompasses the western territories of Ukraine, including several contemporary administrative regions. Historically significant, this region has been shaped by various political entities and cultural influences, making it a vital part of Ukraine's national identity.

title: Yulia Tymoshenko
summary: Yulia Volodymyrivna Tymoshenko is a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the first female [[prime-minister-of-ukraine|Prime Minister of Ukraine]], holding office in 2005 and again from 2007 to 2010. She is known for her leadership in the Batkivshchyna political party and her significant role in Ukraine's political landscape, including her involvement in the Orange Revolution and various presidential elections.

title: Zaporizhian Sich
summary: The Zaporozhian Sich was a semi-autonomous polity and proto-state of the Zaporozhian Cossacks, existing from the 16th to the 18th centuries, primarily in southeastern Ukraine. It played a significant role in the defense of Ukrainian territories against external threats while also being a center of Cossack life and governance.

title: Zaporizhzhia
summary: Zaporizhzhia is a significant city in southeast Ukraine, located on the banks of the Dnieper River and serving as the administrative center of Zaporizhzhia Oblast. With a population of 710,052 as of 2022, it is known for its industrial capabilities, historical significance, and the island of Khortytsia.

title: Zhytomyr
type: city of regional significance of Ukraine
summary: Zhytomyr is a city located in the north of the western part of Ukraine, serving as the administrative center of Zhytomyr Oblast and the surrounding urban hromada. With a population of 261,624 as of 2022, it is a significant transport hub and has a rich historical and cultural heritage.
